architecture.mechanism: The printability and mechanical integrity of polycarbonate are governed by a coupled thermal-kinetic matrix where nozzle temperature and extrusion velocity determine the rate of crystallization and adhesion between layers, and this sensitivity is exacerbated when the part bed or ambient temperature exceeds specific thresholds, leading to delamination or layer skipping if the cooling profile is insufficient.
architecture.intervention: Implement a closed-loop active cooling system that maintains the build platform and immediate surrounding ambient temperature below 35C, or increase the nozzle temperature and reduce the extrusion velocity (increase dwell time) to compensate for the higher baseline thermal energy, ensuring the thermal budget allows for proper interlayer fusion without premature solidification or delamination.
architecture.expected_effect: The thermal gradient between the molten filament and the underlying layer remains within the polymer's rheological window, preventing the "layer skipping" failure mode by ensuring the new layer adheres chemically and mechanically to the previous one rather than slipping or delaminating due to inconsistent viscosity or thermal shock.
architecture.falsification_test: Measure the interlayer shear strength of test coupons printed at 35C ambient with and without the proposed active cooling/parameter adjustment; if the "skipping" persists at the same frequency despite maintaining a constant sub-ambient thermal environment or adjusted viscosity profile, the mechanism is falsified.
